If, however, there simply is an enforced rest, without any intelligent understanding of the trouble, the invalid gets "well" only to drag out a miserable existence or to get very ill again.

arxiv-2109-01890.title: Spectra of Higher Spin Operators on the Sphere
arxiv-2109-01890.creator: Doojin Hong
arxiv-2109-01890.description: Abstract We present explicit formulas for the spectra of higher spin operators ( [ 9 ] ) on the subbundle of the bundle of spinor-valued trace free symmetric tensors that are annihilated by the Clifford multiplication over the standard sphere in odd dimension. In even dimensional case, we give the spectra of the square of such operators.

arxiv-2205-14288.title: Few-shot Subgoal Planning with Language Models
arxiv-2205-14288.creator: Lajanugen Logeswaran, Yao Fu, Moontae Lee, Honglak Lee, LG AI Research, University of Illinois at Chicago, University of Michigan
arxiv-2205-14288.description: Abstract Pre-trained large language models have shown successful progress in many language understanding benchmarks. This work explores the capability of these models to predict actionable plans in real-world environments. Given a text instruction, we show that language priors encoded in pre-trained language models allow us to infer fine-grained subgoal sequences.

arxiv-2206-13123.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Using Feature Disentanglement And GCNs For Medical Image Classification
arxiv-2206-13123.creator: Dwarikanath Mahapatra
arxiv-2206-13123.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dwarikanath Mahapatra. The success of deep learning has set new benchmarks for many medical image analysis tasks. However, deep models often fail to generalize in the presence of distribution shifts between training (source) data and test (target) data. One method commonly employed to counter distribution shifts is domain adaptation: using samples from the target domain to learn to account for shifted distributions.

arxiv-2212-03015.title: Lattice QCD at non-zero temperature and density
arxiv-2212-03015.creator: F. Karsch
arxiv-2212-03015.description: Abstract Soon after the formulation of Quantum Chromodynamics in 1972 its regularization on Euclidean space-time lattices had been introduced by Kenneth Wilson [ 1 ] . This paved ground for numerical studies of non-perturbative aspects of QCD, first shown by Michael Creutz [ 2 ] .

arxiv-2401-06003.title: TRIPS: Trilinear Point Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
arxiv-2401-06003.creator: Linus Franke , Darius Rückert , Laura Fink and Marc Stamminger Visual Computing Erlangen, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, Germany {firstname.lastname}@fau.de
arxiv-2401-06003.description: Abstract Point-based radiance field rendering has demonstrated impressive results for novel view synthesis, offering a compelling blend of rendering quality and computational efficiency. However, also latest approaches in this domain are not without their shortcomings. 3D Gaussian Splatting [ KKLD23 ] struggles when tasked with rendering highly detailed scenes, due to blurring and cloudy artifacts.

arxiv-2401-07691.title: Privacy-Aware Single-Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) using Bilinear Group Accumulators in Batch Mode
arxiv-2401-07691.creator: William J Buchanan 1 , Sam Grierson 1 and Daniel Uribe 2 1 Blockpass ID Lab, Edinburgh Napier University, Edinburgh, UK 2 GenoVerse.io { b.buchanan, s.grierson2 } @napier.ac.uk
arxiv-2401-07691.description: Abstract Biometric data is often highly sensitive, and a leak of this data can lead to serious privacy breaches. Some of the most sensitive of this type of data relates to the usage of DNA data on individuals. A leak of this type of data without consent could lead to privacy breaches of data protection laws.

arxiv-2510-05016.title: Large Language Models Achieve Gold Medal Performance at the International Olympiad on Astronomy & Astrophysics (IOAA)
arxiv-2510-05016.creator: Lucas Carrit Delgado Pinheiro, Ziru Chen, Bruno Caixeta Piazza, Ness Shroff, Yingbin Liang, Yuan-Sen Ting, Huan Sun
arxiv-2510-05016.description: Abstract While task-specific demonstrations show early success in applying large language models (LLMs) to automate some astronomical research tasks, they only provide incomplete views of all necessary capabilities in solving astronomy problems, calling for more thorough understanding of LLMs’ strengths and limitations.

arxiv-2602-09072.title: Circular Super patterns and Zigzag constructions
arxiv-2602-09072.creator: M Hariprasad , Raisa Dsouza
arxiv-2602-09072.description: Abstract Abstract: In this article, we introduce the notion of a circular k -superpatterns, permutations that contain all k length patterns upto rotation equivalence. We present a construction of circular superpattern using the linear (k-1) superpattern, explicitly giving the upper bound on the length.

plos-pone-0002280.creator: Maha Saeed, Will Roeffen, Neal Alexander et al.
plos-pone-0002280.description: PLOS ONE research article. The asexual blood stages of the human malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum produce highly immunogenic polymorphic antigens that are expressed on the surface of the host cell. In contrast, few studies have examined the surface of the gametocyte-infected erythrocyte. We used flow

pmc-10548137.title: Uncovering the Achilles heel of genetic heterogeneity: machine learning-based classification and immunological properties of necroptosis clusters in Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-10548137.creator: Huangwei Wei, Chunle Wu, Yulin Yuan, Lichuan Lai
pmc-10548137.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) is an age-associated neurodegenerative disease, and the currently available diagnostic modalities and therapeutic agents are unsatisfactory due to its high clinical heterogeneity. Necroptosis is a common type of programmed cell death that has been shown to be activated in AD.

pmc-10559346.title: Exploring the knowledge, practices & determinants of antibiotic self-medication among bangladeshi university students in the era of COVID-19: A cross-sectional study
pmc-10559346.creator: Abrar Wahab, Mohammad Morshad Alam, Shahriar Hasan, Sangeeta Halder, Md Obayed Ullah, Ahmed Hossain
pmc-10559346.description: Self-medication with antibiotics is a growing public health concern. Antibiotics are easily accessible on requested from pharmacies throughout the majority of developing countries. The present study aimed to determine the prevalence of self-medication with antibiotics among university students in Bangladesh, as well as to evaluate their knowledge and practices related to antibiotics and its resistance.

pmc-11350654.title: A New Species of Cyrtodactylus tibetanus Group (Reptilia: Squamata: Gekkonidae) from Xizang Autonomous Region, China †
pmc-11350654.creator: Shun Ma, Sheng-Chao Shi, Tian-Yu Qian, Lu-Lu Sui, Bin Wang, Jian-Ping Jiang, Andreas Maletzky
pmc-11350654.description: Simple SummaryMore than 350 species (32 species groups) of Cyrtodactylus Gray, 1827, are reported currently, with a wide distribution from Himalaya, South Asia, Southeast Asia, to Melanesia. Cyrtodactylus tibetanus group, as the earliest Cyrtodactylus diverging clade, are endemic to the Yarlung–Tsangpo River Basin of Tibetan Plateau, only containing two species: C. tibetanus and C. zhaoermii.

pmc-11511574.title: Ensemble and Gossip Learning-Based Framework for Intrusion Detection System in Vehicle-to-Everything Communication Environment
pmc-11511574.creator: Muhammad Nadeem Ali, Muhammad Imran, Ihsan Ullah, Ghulam Musa Raza, Hye-Young Kim, Byung-Seo Kim, Weizhi Meng
pmc-11511574.description: Autonomous vehicles are revolutionizing the future of intelligent transportation systems by integrating smart and intelligent onboard units (OBUs) that minimize human intervention. These vehicles can communicate with their environment and one another, sharing critical information such as emergency alerts or media content. However, this communication infrastructure is susceptible to cyber-attacks, necessitating robust mechanisms for detection and defense.

pmc-11655522.title: A root nodule microbiome sequencing data set from red alder (Alnus rubra Bong.)
pmc-11655522.creator: Callum J. Bell, Johnny A. Sena, Diego A. Fajardo, Evan M. Lavelle, Michael A. Costa, Barrington Herman, Laurence B. Davin, Norman G. Lewis, Alison M. Berry
pmc-11655522.description: There have been frequent reports of more than one strain of the nitrogen-fixing symbiont, Frankia, in the same root nodule of plants in the genus Alnus, but quantitative assessments of their relative contributions have not been made to date. Neither has the diversity of other microbes, having potential functional roles in symbiosis, been systematically evaluated.

pmc-12427232.title: Spatiotemporal Patterns of Fish Diversity in the Waters Around the Five West Sea Islands of South Korea: Integrating Bottom Trawl and Environmental DNA (eDNA) Methods
pmc-12427232.creator: Young-Ji Yoo, So-Yeon An, Seung-Hwan Lee, Soo-Jeong Lee, Woo-Seok Gwak
pmc-12427232.description: Simple SummaryThis study presents the first parallel survey using traditional bottom trawling and environmental DNA (eDNA) analysis to investigate fish species around the Five West Sea Islands of South Korea. Over three seasonal sampling periods, fish community composition was closely linked to water temperature changes.

pmc-12476458.title: Unpaid care, time taken off work and healthcare costs before and after partner bereavement among same-gender and different-gender partners: A national population-based study
pmc-12476458.creator: Katherine Bristowe, Peter May, Alexandra Pitman, Jingjing Jiang, Liadh Timmins, Michael King, Debbie Braybrook, Steve Marshall, Elizabeth Day, Paul Clift, Ruth Rose, Katherine Johnson, Kathryn Almack, Richard Harding
pmc-12476458.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background:Recent research has demonstrated higher levels of psychological distress for bereaved same-gender partners compared to different-gender partners. pmc-12566221.title: Review: Sustainable Biosorbent and Biopolymeric Materials for Heavy Metal Adsorption—Advances, Challenges, and Perspectives
pmc-12566221.creator: André Lamounier Caixeta, Ana Carolina Nunes da Silva, Sarah Kalli Silva da Silva, Matheus de Carvalho Dias, Camila Monteiro Cholant, Tiago Moreno Volkmer, André Luiz Missio, Amanda Dantas de Oliveira, Mateus Meneguetti Ferrer, Yasir Anwar, Sabir Khan
pmc-12566221.description: The contamination of water resources by heavy metals poses a serious environmental risk, and conventional treatment methods face significant limitations. This review addresses the issue by presenting a critical analysis of the development of sustainable biosorbent and biopolymeric materials for heavy metal adsorption, highlighting advances, challenges, and future perspectives.

pmc-12643746.title: Bidirectional 2-sample Mendelian randomization study of the causal relationship between hypothyroidism and cardiovascular diseases
pmc-12643746.creator: Jianing Chi, Sheng Qiu, Wenqiang Ma, Guanyu Yan, Yanhua Xue
pmc-12643746.description: A bidirectional 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was used to investigate the causal relationship between hypothyroidism and multiple types of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). Single nucleotide polymorphisms strongly associated with hypothyroidism and 4 CVDs (myocardial infarction, coronary artery disease, heart failure [HF], hypertension) were extracted from genome-wide association study summary data as instrumental variables, excluding linkage disequilibrium.

pmc-12660402.title: A noninvasive machine learning model using a complete blood count for screening of primary vitreoretinal lymphoma
pmc-12660402.creator: Shengjie Li, Jiazhen Cao, Danhui Li, Jun Ren, Jianing Wu, Yingzhu Li, Mengyu Zhang, Henggui Hu, Yunxiao Song, Jie Cheng, Ming Guan, Wenjun Cao
pmc-12660402.description: Primary vitreoretinal lymphoma (PVRL) is a rare and aggressive intraocular malignancy that is frequently misdiagnosed because of its nonspecific early manifestations and the lack of effective screening tools. We conduct a multicentre case–control study including 255 PVRL patients and 292 controls to develop a machine learning–based screening model using complete blood count data.

pmc-12749512.title: Digital fatigue and academic resilience among university students with grit and flexibility as mediators
pmc-12749512.creator: Ran An, Guanghui Qian, Ayesha Mumtaz, Khalid Abdullah Alotaibi, Xiu Wang
pmc-12749512.description: The increasing reliance on digital technologies in higher education has led to a rise in digital fatigue, which negatively impacts students’ academic resilience. While psychological traits such as grit and psychological flexibility enhance resilience, their individual and combined effects on digital fatigue remain underexplored, particularly in Chinese academic settings.

pmc-12752325.title: Using MediaPipe to track upper-limb reaching movements after stroke: a proof-of-principle study
pmc-12752325.creator: Vaidehi Wagh, Matthew W Scott, Justin W Andrushko, Christina B Jones, Beverley C Larssen, Lara A Boyd, Sarah N Kraeutner
pmc-12752325.description: Emerging work supports the use of artificial intelligence-based markerless motion capture systems to complement standardized clinical measures when assessing post-stroke motor recovery. MediaPipe Pose Landmarker is an open-sourced, machine learning tool, requiring only one camera, which can be used to track upper limb movements and quantify kinematics.

pmc-12809979.title: Smartphone-based application for cognitive behavioral therapy of panic disorder: a feasibility study with volunteers reporting past panic attacks
pmc-12809979.creator: Emre Cem Esen, Hayriye Baykan
pmc-12809979.description: BackgroundPanic disorder affects up to 5% of people. It is often treated with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and antidepressants. However, access to CBT remains limited because of psychiatrist and psychologist shortages and long wait times. Digital health solutions have emerged to address this gap. Still, many applications lack personalization and professional oversight.

pmc-12983628.title: Development of a liver stiffness measurement-based nomogram model to identify early CKD risk in patients with MAFLD
pmc-12983628.creator: Dejin Huang, Xiaoxuan Ma, Qingchen Gao, Xiaolong Shen, Tongtong Yu, Rongqi Wang
pmc-12983628.description: ObjectiveTo identify independent relevant factors for chronic kidney disease (CKD) in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) and to develop and validate a nomogram-based risk diagnostic model for MAFLD-CKD incorporating liver stiffness measurement (LSM).MethodsClinical data from 3,154 patients with fatty liver disease attending our hospital between January 2024 and September 2025 were collected.

pmc-13222342.title: Identification and characterisation of an elusive bacterial enzyme system for chloromethane dehalogenation
pmc-13222342.creator: Jasmin Bernhardt, Lukas K. R. Hofmann, Paul Klemm, Nicole Paczia, Olivier N. Lemaire, Stéphane Vuilleumier, Tristan Wagner, Julia M. Kurth
pmc-13222342.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Chloromethane, a toxic gas primarily produced naturally, contributes to stratospheric ozone destruction. The anaerobic acetogen Acetobacterium dehalogenans can utilise chloromethane as a carbon and energy source, but the associated dehalogenase/methyltransferase has remained elusive. Through comparative transcriptomics we identify a gene cluster, cdmBCA, which encodes a corrinoid-dependent methyltransferase system distinct from the characterised Cmu system used for chloromethane degradation in aerobic methylotrophs. Biochemical characterisation reveals that the Cdm system reacts with other haloalkanes, but not with methoxylated aromatics, unlike closely related O-demethylases.

pmc-13481501.title: Integrative single-cell transcriptomic and epitranscriptomic analysis of the RBM15–m6A–IL10 regulatory axis in psoriatic keratinocytes
pmc-13481501.creator: Mo Li, Yuyao Jiang, Chengcheng Zhu, Meng Zhao, Dan Wang
pmc-13481501.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPsoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disorder hallmarked by keratinocyte hyperproliferation and impaired apoptosis. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification is emerging as a critical regulator of inflammatory gene expression. RNA-binding motif protein 15 (RBM15), a core m6A methyltransferase complex adaptor, promotes oncogenic processes across tissue types; however, its role in psoriatic keratinocyte biology and its potential regulation of interleukin-10 (IL-10)—a pivotal anti-apoptotic and immunomodulatory cytokine—remain unexplored.MethodsSingle-cell RNA sequencing data from a publicly deposited psoriasis dataset (GSE248121; 23,851 cells from two paired libraries)
